open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text:
Ignored names are not reported, ignored folders are not entered, and an entry the listing shows as a symbolic link is neither reported nor followed.

Syncthing may change the folder during a scan, so a scan is not a view of one instant. Each rule applies
to what its step finds when it runs
open_points.question: If a listed subfolder becomes a symbolic link before traversal, is it silently skipped or is the scan refused with folder_unavailable?
options: Skip it because the traversal step now finds a symbolic link
Refuse the whole scan with folder_unavailable because the listed subfolder can no longer be safely listed
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the whole scan with folder_unavailable.

witness.initial: The scan lists subfolder albums as an ordinary directory; an external directory contains outside.jpg.
events: Syncthing replaces albums with a symbolic link to the external directory before the scan traverses it.
The scanner reaches albums.
outcomes: The scanner skips albums and completes successfully without outside.jpg.
The scanner refuses the entire scan with folder_unavailable.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees either a complete scan answer or a folder_unavailable refusal.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: an empty, absolute, unnormalised or parent-climbing name
open_points.question: Does “unnormalised” mean only a lexically non-canonical path, or also a filename whose Unicode spelling is not in a normalization form, despite A3 saying names are compared exactly without Unicode normalisation?
options: Only lexical path forms such as repeated separators or dot segments are unnormalised
Unicode-decomposed filenames are also unnormalised and must be refused
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as lexical path normalization only and accept an exact Unicode-decomposed filename when that file exists.

witness.initial: The photo folder contains a regular JPEG named with the decomposed spelling café.jpg, and the request uses those exact code points.
events: The caller requests delivery using that exact relative name.
The delivery evaluates A3 condition 1 and the INV-02 Required tests item.
outcomes: The exact existing name passes because Unicode normalization is expressly not performed.
The name fails with NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT because the test's “unnormalised” category includes decomposed Unicode.
witness.observer: The caller sees placed versus failed.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: INV-02: a delivery opens only a path that meets condition 1 of A3 rule 5.
open_points.question: Does “meets condition 1” mean that the path satisfies the listed failure condition, or that it passes the condition and therefore does not satisfy it?
options: Only paths that satisfy the failure condition may be opened
Only paths that do not satisfy the failure condition may be opened
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it as “does not meet condition 1,” so only validated paths may be opened.

witness.initial: One request names an existing regular file and another names a symbolic-link path.
events: The delivery applies A3 rule 5 condition 1.
It decides whether either path may be opened.
outcomes: A literal reading permits opening only the invalid symbolic-link path.
The apparent intended reading permits opening only the existing regular file.
witness.observer: A filesystem access monitor and the caller see which path is opened and whether delivery succeeds.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: INV-02: an empty, absolute, unnormalised or parent-climbing name, an ignored name at any level, a folder, and a path through a symbolic link each fail with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure and add no file except the project lock (`test_a_name_a_scan_would_not_report_is_not_delivered`).
open_points.question: Must the Required tests item show that each rejected path is never opened, rather than only checking its answer and durable writes?
options: Instrument file opening and assert that none of the rejected paths is opened
Treat the failure answer and absence of new durable files as sufficient evidence
open_points.default_guess: Instrument opening and assert that rejected paths are not opened.

witness.initial: An ignored regular file exists and can record or expose read access without causing a stored write.
events: A delivery implementation opens and reads the file.
It then returns NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT and writes only the project lock.
outcomes: The stated Required tests assertions pass even though INV-02 is violated.
A test that observes open calls fails and proves the invariant.
witness.observer: A filesystem access monitor sees the read; the current described test and caller do not.

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text: delivering content that has no placement under the name of a conflict copy fails with the NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT member of = models.PlacementFailure, adds no file except the project lock and changes no existing file (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`)
open_points.question: How must the test demonstrate INV-19's requirement that a new placement never reads a conflict copy?
options: Observe file-open or file-read calls and assert that the conflict copy is never read
Check only the failure answer and resulting filesystem state
open_points.default_guess: Observe file access and assert that the conflict copy is never opened or read.

witness.initial: An unplaced conflict copy contains a valid image.
events: The implementation opens and reads its bytes.
It discards them, returns NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT, and changes no file except the project lock.
outcomes: All behavior named by the Required tests item holds while INV-19 is violated.
A read-observing test detects the violation.
witness.observer: A filesystem access monitor sees the read; the caller and the described state assertions do not.

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text:
After condition 5 a stored image may remain without a record: no caller has received
   its reference, and a repeated delivery writes it again and completes the placement.

Deliver one chosen photo | a prepared image in the Portal store, its reference and the publication body | a photo that cannot be delivered is reported with its reason and nothing is written; a file whose content differs from the chosen one is not placed
open_points.question: When record writing fails after the stored image was written, must the image remain as A3 permits, or must nothing remain as the State 0 action promises?
options: Keep the unreferenced stored image and return failed
Remove or roll back the stored image so nothing durable was written
open_points.default_guess: Follow the more specific A3 recovery rule and permit the unreferenced stored image to remain.

witness.initial: No placement or stored image exists for the requested project and source.
events: The delivery successfully writes the stored image.
Writing the placement record fails.
The service returns failed with UNREADABLE_FILE.
outcomes: A3 leaves the stored image without a record.
State 0 requires that nothing was written, so no stored image remains.
witness.observer: The binary-store operator sees whether the image remains.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: A file's modification time is converted to the same form before it is compared or delivered
open_points.question: Which metadata observation supplies the modification instant, and how many times may one scan or delivery read it when the file changes during the operation?
options: Read it once from pre-open path metadata
Read it once from the opened file descriptor
Read it more than once and use a specified first or last reading
open_points.default_guess: Read it once from the opened file descriptor and reuse that value.

witness.initial: A JPEG without a usable camera date has modification time T1.
events: The delivery reads path metadata.
Syncthing changes the file's modification time to T2 before it is opened, without changing its bytes.
The delivery opens and prepares the file.
outcomes: The delivered photo moment is T1 from the pre-open metadata.
The delivered photo moment is T2 from metadata of the opened file.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal see different photo_date values.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.question: Which exact ISO 8601 serialization is required for a UTC datetime without an offset, including separator and whether six fractional digits are always emitted?
options: Use T and always emit exactly six fractional digits with no suffix
Use any ISO 8601-compatible naive-datetime spelling, including a space separator or omitted zero fraction
Append a UTC designator despite saying the datetime has no offset
open_points.default_guess: Use `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffff` with exactly six fractional digits and no offset or Z suffix.

witness.initial: The clock returns a naive UTC datetime whose microsecond value is zero.
events: A mark is created and marked_at is serialized.
outcomes: The stored value is another ISO 8601 form such as `2026-11-18 12:00:00`.
witness.observer: A reader of the state record sees different bytes and may parse or compare them differently.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
open_points.question: Must the Required tests item also show the clock-read count for marks refused before the read point, refused after it, and replayed, so INV-13 is established on every mark path?
options: Test successful, early-refused, late-refused, and replayed marks separately
Test one successful mark only and infer the other mark paths
open_points.default_guess: Test every listed mark path and assert counts of zero or one as A7 rule 2 specifies.

witness.initial: A publication mark already exists for the source.
events: The caller repeats the mark with the same photo_id.
An implementation reads the clock twice but returns the existing mark without writing.
The described successful-mark, scan, delivery, and health checks run.
outcomes: The described checks can pass although the replay path violates INV-13.
A replay-specific counting-clock check fails on the second read.
witness.observer: The counting clock or its test sees the difference; the caller receives the same replay answer.
